Motion to IEC 
 Monday, July 6, 2026 
 Speeding up the College Streetcar Study 
 Summary 
 More than half of Ward 11 residents do not have private vehicles and depend on transit and active
 transportation. Key transit arteries in Ward 11 include the busy Dundas, College, Bathurst and Spadina
 streetcar lines. International research has shown that Toronto streetcars are the slowest in the world, due
 primarily to the vehicles being stuck in mixed traffic and lacking appropriate transit priority. Transit priority
 measures (including signal changes, and parking and turn restrictions) that have been rolled out on Spadina,
 Bathurst and Dundas have demonstrated that considerable improvements are possible when transit gets the
 priority it deserves. Now it’s time to learn what is possible and achievable on College Street. 
 Recommendations 
 It is recommended that: 
 1. Infrastructure and Environment Committee request the General Manager, Transportation, Services,
 in collaboration with the Chief Executive Officer, Toronto Transit Commission, to consult the
 community and to report back to Infrastructure and Environment Committee in Q1 2027 with
 recommendations how to improve the speed and reliability of the College Streetcar through transit
 priority measures that are within the control of the city. 
 Councillor Dianne Saxe 
 Ward 11, University–Rosedale
